body:
PR628's balanced cyclic inverse can use **cubic sufficient precision with arbitrary dirty arrays**:

```text
max(p, incoming_grid_bits) + O(m + r^3)
```

The dispatcher, rounded leaves, quadratic leaf count and logarithmic number of borrowed arrays are unchanged. No reserved zero bits or clean length-L array are required. **No new κ.**

The new free-algebra induction shows that every ideal prefix and inverse prefix is a sum of ordered products with no repeated factor occurrence. Their coefficient row sum is at most `2*3^ceil(log2 n)`. Applying #862's common-isometry complementary-factor bound to these products, then #877's nonlinear perturbation argument, gives the cubic precision bound. Both source and borrowed arrays still restore exactly; the rounded increment may depend on the initial dirt.

At radix 64, p=128 and initial magnitude at most 2^20, the explicit fractional-bit budget is **1,162,553**, versus **73,245,212** in #877. Both schedules have **4,000 leaves and six dirty arrays**. These are conservative sufficient bounds, not minimum precision or measured performance. Cubic coefficient preparation uses #862's inherited full-inverse estimate; every leaf pass, inverse call, validation, source access, arithmetic and routing charge remains.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-cubic-precision/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/dirty-cubic-precision/test_package.py
```

Validation on frozen source:

- macOS arm64 Python 3.11.15 and Linux aarch64 Python 3.14.8 produced byte-identical complete mathematical receipts. Linux ran the entire package read-only, outside a repository checkout.
- 5,220 exact integer budgets, checked by a separate recurrence/inequality implementation.
- 142 free noncommuting polynomial traces through 256 factors: 652,654 leaf boundaries, checking prefixes and inverse prefixes. Another 128 words match the frozen dispatcher.
- 18 dense traces, 66 separate Gauss-Jordan inverse checks and 5,104 directly reconstructed intervals.
- 80 actual rounded kernel cases, all with nonzero rounding error and **an odd lowest working bit in every initial scalar word**, including borrowed storage. They check all 6,032 leaf boundaries, dense exact errors, true-kernel perturbation, source/dirty restoration and inverse cancellation.
- Thirteen mathematical controls, eight package-binding controls per platform, read-only relocation, exact source Git-blob comparisons and unchanged selected-record integrity passed. Full per-platform receipts and logs are included.

Sources are pinned and retained unchanged: #628 `0768f97d…`, #877 `80a60c0d…`, and #862 `57e06591…`, including the original #621 proof/notice lineage. Credit Chafik Boukhalfa, Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), Ali Romman, 0xkilgore and the retained predecessors. #896's concurrent formalization concerns complete nonlinear restoration and ordered products; it explicitly supplies no precision estimate and is not imported here.

All factors must use the same immutable unit-weighted permutation and direction, with phase data distinct from mutable arrays. The conclusion rests on the written universal induction plus inherited analytic, leaf and supplied-preparation hypotheses. It does not supply a bit-reversible compiler, common-label/Clifford word, physical layout, complete transform or multiplication reduction. Selected construction and `upstream/` are unchanged. Hosted CI is configured for full Python 3.11/3.14 replays; no hosted success is claimed by the prepublication records.

Prepared by Chafik Boukhalfa with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. Separate arithmetic paths are not independent human review or a formal verification of the full theorem.
title: Research: cubic precision for cyclic inverses with arbitrary dirty arrays (no new kappa)
